items.title: Bob Rosengarden interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, October 6, 1996
items.q: I imitated him. I did my mimicking. I imitated what he did. But he meant it.

ctx.x: So it wasn’t one of the players.

No. Dick Gibson was, is still alive, out in Denver. An impresario. I mean he was a businessman who did very well and he loved Hag and he loved Yank Lawson. Yank was quite a drinker in those days. And so Yank would mumble a lot, and Hag was just Mount Pleasant. And I played in that band at various times. Cliff Leeman was the first drummer. And Cliff did a wonderful job for that band, much better than I did. I imitated him. I did my mimicking. I imitated what he did. But he meant it. And I enjoyed playing with that…
You’ve been a part of so many interesting ensembles, the “New York Repertory.”

items.title: 68087_Cliff Leeman oral history interview
items.q: Let's see, there's myself on drums, and Duke Hanna, and Mousey Alexander, Bobby Rosengarden - that's a motley crew!

ctx.x: I've done a bunch of recordings with Flip, appeared with him 6 weeks last year at Michael's Pub in New York -- also jazz concerts around New York, and Milt Hinton was in on some of those. Milt, you were with me in Michael's Pub, weren't you, with Flip, among others?

To continue with the artists at the Odessa party, we also had on that same program, on trombones, one that's always with us, the superb Carl Fontana. We had Lou McGarity until his death. And a wonderful Texas trombonist, Ashley Alexander, Jr. We had Ed Hubl on trombone -- another really great unsung hero musically. Let's see, there's myself on drums, and Duke Hanna, and Mousey Alexander, Bobby Rosengarden - that's a motley crew!
On reeds - clarinet is Johnnie Mince, Peanuts
